An expected [wave of technology initial public offerings](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/14/technology/ai-ipo-openai-anthropic-spacex.html) is kicking into high gear. Cerebras [initially filed to list its shares](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/30/technology/cerebras-ai-chips-ipo.html) in the fall of 2024, before raising additional funding and [withdrawing its offering plans](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/03/cerebras-withdraws-ipo-ai.html) without providing a reason. This month, SpaceX, Elon Musk’s rocket and satellite maker, which is valued at more than $1 trillion, [filed to list its shares](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/01/technology/spacex-ipo-elon-musk.html) in what is likely to be one of the largest-ever public offerings. The A.I. companies [OpenAI and Anthropic](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/14/technology/ai-ipo-openai-anthropic-spacex.html) have also taken early steps to go public. news.raw_snippet: # AI startup Cursor in talks to raise $2 billion funding round at valuation of over $50 billion. * Artificial intelligence startup Cursor is in talks to raise a $2 billion fundraising round at an over $50 billion valuation, which does not include the investment, a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. * The funding round underscores the venture capital industry's enthusiasm for startups specializing in AI coding agents that can complete various software development tasks for users. Artificial intelligence startup Cursor is in talks to raise a $2 billion fundraising round at an over $50 billion valuation, which does not include the investment, a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. The funding round underscores the venture capital industry's enthusiasm for startups specializing in AI coding agents that can complete a range of software development tasks for users. Although Cursor was among the first major startups to focus on AI coding agents, other companies, such as Google, Anthropic and OpenAI, have since debuted similar tools.

He reckoned that if that was the case, then Elon Musk, one of the biggest proponents of AI, may be the first to be replaced. Take-Two Interactive's CEO Strauss Zelnick believes that Elon Musk would be the first one to lose his job if AI replaces all humans. Take-Two Interactive’s CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is confident that artificial intelligence (AI) will not take away your job. So much so, that Strauss insisted that when the day comes of AI replacing all humans, the first one to lose their job would be the world’s richest person, Elon Musk. He said, "If AI were to take anyone's job, wouldn't it take his [Elon Musk's] job? Elon Musk is one of the most vocal advocates for AI. Musk has often claimed that AI will replace all humans in the workforce, making us free from the need to work.
